Fix $\gamma>1$. In one space dimension the conserved state is
$U=(\rho,m,E)\in\mathbb R^3$, where $\rho$ is density, $m$ momentum, and
$E$ total energy per unit volume. The **admissible-state set** is the open set
$$\mathcal G_\gamma=\{(\rho,m,E):\rho>0,\ E>m^2/(2\rho)\}.$$
The ideal-gas pressure on this set is
$$p(U)=(\gamma-1)\left(E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}\right)>0,$$
the velocity is $u=m/\rho$, and the flux is
$$F(U)=\left(m,\frac{m^2}{\rho}+p,\frac{m}{\rho}(E+p)\right).$$
The sound speed is $c=\sqrt{\gamma p/\rho}$. These definitions apply only
on $\mathcal G_\gamma$; a state with nonpositive density or nonpositive
internal energy is inadmissible. The set is open because $\rho$ and
$E-m^2/(2\rho)$ are continuous on $\rho>0$ and the inequalities are strict;
all displayed flux functions are smooth on this domain.

Fix $\gamma>1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, and use the state variables and internal
energy density from [[def-ideal-gas-euler-state-and-pressure]]. Define the
**positive-margin set**
$$K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}:=\left\{(\rho,m,E):\rho\ge\varepsilon,\quad E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}\ge\varepsilon\right\}.$$
Every member has positive density and positive pressure. Closedness and
convexity are proved in
[[prop-pe03-euler-state-and-margin-domains-are-convex-and-closed]]; those properties are not
being inferred from this definition alone.

derivations.claim: Let $U_k=(\rho_k,m_k,E_k)\in\mathcal G_\gamma$ for $k=1,2$ and $0\le\theta\le1$. Put $\rho_\theta=\theta\rho_1+(1-\theta)\rho_2$ and similarly define $m_\theta,E_\theta$. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz applied to $m_\theta=\sqrt{\theta\rho_1}(\sqrt\theta m_1/\sqrt{\rho_1})+\sqrt{(1-\theta)\rho_2}(\sqrt{1-\theta}m_2/\sqrt{\rho_2})$ gives $m_\theta^2\le\rho_\theta\bigl(\theta m_1^2/\rho_1+(1-\theta)m_2^2/\rho_2\bigr)$. Thus $\rho_\theta>0$ and $E_\theta-m_\theta^2/(2\rho_\theta)\ge\theta(E_1-m_1^2/(2\rho_1))+(1-\theta)(E_2-m_2^2/(2\rho_2))>0$. Therefore $\mathcal G_\gamma$ is convex.

For $U_1,U_2\in K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$, the weighted Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in step 1.1 gives $\rho_\theta\ge\varepsilon$ and $E_\theta-m_\theta^2/(2\rho_\theta)\ge\theta\varepsilon+(1-\theta)\varepsilon=\varepsilon$. Hence $K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$ is convex.

If $U_n=(\rho_n,m_n,E_n)\in K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$ converges to $U=(\rho,m,E)$, then $\rho\ge\varepsilon>0$ and continuity of $(\rho,m,E)\mapsto E-m^2/(2\rho)$ on $\rho\ge\varepsilon$ gives $E-m^2/(2\rho)\ge\varepsilon$. Thus $U\in K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$, proving closedness.

From [F1], direct substitution in $U+\delta F(U)$ gives $\rho_\delta=\rho(1+\delta u)=\rho x$, $m_\delta=\rho u(1+\delta u)+\delta p$, and $E_\delta=E+\delta u(E+p)$. $S_L<S_R$. A signal speed means the propagation speed of one wave in the
particular Riemann solution being approximated. If the HLL model is used as an
enclosing approximation to that fan, its admissibility hypothesis is that
every such speed lies in $[S_L,S_R]$; this definition supplies no general
wave-speed bound.
Set $f_L=f(u_L)$ and $f_R=f(u_R)$. The HLL flux is
$$\widehat f_{\rm HLL}=\begin{cases}f_L,&0\le S_L,\\\dfrac{S_Rf_L-S_Lf_R+S_LS_R(u_R-u_L)}{S_R-S_L},&S_L<0<S_R,\\f_R,&S_R\le0.\end{cases}$$
In the middle case the model has three constant regions separated by the two
waves $S_L,S_R$ and one intermediate state. The wave-speed enclosure is a
separate hypothesis whenever an approximation claim uses it.

When $S_L<0<S_R$, the HLL intermediate state
$$u_* =\frac{S_Ru_R-S_Lu_L-(f_R-f_L)}{S_R-S_L}$$
together with the assigned model flux
$$f_* = f_L+S_L(u_*-u_L)$$
satisfies the two model balances
$$f_*-f_L=S_L(u_*-u_L),\qquad f_R-f_*=S_R(u_R-u_*).$$
This $f_*$ is the middle formula in [[def-hll-two-wave-flux]]. In general
$f_*\ne f(u_*)$, even when $u_*\in G$; the model is not asserted to be a
weak solution of the original conservation law. For equal states

$$U_j^{new}=U_j-\nu\bigl(\widehat f_{\rm HLL}(U_j,U_{j+1})-\widehat f_{\rm HLL}(U_{j-1},U_j)\bigr).$$

Let $m,N\ge1$, let $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be a state domain, and let
$\Phi:\mathcal A^N\to\mathcal A^N$ be a one-step update on $N$ cell states.
A set $K\subseteq\mathcal A$ is **convex** if
$\theta U+(1-\theta)V\in K$ for every $U,V\in K$ and $\theta\in[0,1]$.
It is a **convex invariant domain for $\Phi$** if it is convex and
$\Phi(K^N)\subseteq K^N$. The word invariant refers only to this stated
one-step map and its stated admissible inputs; it asserts no invariance for a
different flux, time integrator, or exact Riemann evolution.

Use the first-order HLL update of
[[def-pe03-first-order-hll-finite-volume-update]]. At a face with left and right
states $U_L,U_R$, supplied speeds $S_L<0<S_R$, and physical flux values
$F_L=F(U_L),F_R=F(U_R)$, define
$$U_*:=\frac{S_RU_R-S_LU_L-(F_R-F_L)}{S_R-S_L}.$$
If the one-sided CFL bounds $2\nu(-S_L)\le1$ and $2\nu S_R\le1$ hold, the
averages of the HLL fan over the adjacent left and right half-cells are,
respectively,
$$A^-=(1-2\nu(-S_L))U_L+2\nu(-S_L)U_*,\qquad A^+=(1-2\nu S_R)U_R+2\nu S_RU_*.$$
For every cell $i$, the updated mean satisfies
$$U_i^+=\frac12\left(A^+_{i-1/2}+A^-_{i+1/2}\right),$$
where each face uses its own supplied speeds and intermediate state.

derivations.claim: At each face, the stated HLL fan-average hypothesis gives $A^-,A^+\in K$. In the sufficient intermediate-state case, the CFL bounds make the coefficients in each formula of [F2] nonnegative and sum to one, so convexity and $U_L,U_R,U_*\in K$ give the same conclusion.

By [F2], $U_i^+=\tfrac12(A^+_{i-1/2}+A^-_{i+1/2})$. This is a convex combination of two members of $K$, so $U_i^+\in K$ for every cell. The argument is one-step and uses only the supplied HLL speeds and the explicit CFL bounds.

Use the conservation-system convention of
[[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]]: on an open convex state
domain $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, the flux is $F:\mathcal A\to\mathbb R^m$.
A **convex entropy pair** is a pair $(\eta,q)$ with $\eta\in C^2(\mathcal A)$,
$q\in C^1(\mathcal A)$, positive-semidefinite Hessian $D^2\eta$, and
$$Dq(U)=D\eta(U)\,DF(U)\qquad(U\in\mathcal A).$$
The **entropy variable** is the column vector $v(U)=\nabla\eta(U)$; gradients
are represented as columns, so the compatibility equation above means
$\nabla q(U)=DF(U)^T v(U)$. The **entropy potential** is
$\psi(U)=v(U)^T F(U)-q(U)$. This definition does not assert that every convex
$\eta$ admits a flux $q$; the compatibility equation is part of the hypothesis.

Let $(\eta,q)$ be a convex entropy pair on an open domain $\mathcal A$, with
entropy variable $v$ and potential $\psi$ as in
[[def-pe03-system-entropy-pair-and-potential]]. A continuous two-point flux
$F^{ec}:\mathcal A\times\mathcal A\to\mathbb R^m$ is **entropy-conservative
in Tadmor's sense** if it is consistent and symmetric,
$F^{ec}(U,U)=F(U)$, and satisfies the exact jump identity
$$\bigl(v(U_R)-v(U_L)\bigr)^T F^{ec}(U_L,U_R)=\psi(U_R)-\psi(U_L)$$
for every pair $U_L,U_R\in\mathcal A$. This definition asserts no existence
for a prescribed entropy pair.

Let $(\eta,q)$ be an entropy pair with entropy variable $v$ and potential
$\psi$, and let $F^{ec}$ be a consistent entropy-conservative flux as in
[[def-pe03-tadmor-entropy-conservative-flux]]. For each pair
$(U_L,U_R)\in\mathcal A^2$, choose a symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix
$D(U_L,U_R)\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$. The associated **entropy-stable
dissipative flux** is
$$F^{es}(U_L,U_R):=F^{ec}(U_L,U_R)-\frac12D(U_L,U_R)(v(U_R)-v(U_L)).$$
Positive semidefinite means $z^TD(U_L,U_R)z\ge0$ for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$.
No fully discrete time-step property is included.

derivations.claim: At a face, [F2]–[F3] give $[v]^TF^{es}=[\psi]-\tfrac12[v]^TD[v]\le[\psi]$, since $[v]^TD[v]\ge0$. This uses only positive semidefiniteness, including the case where the jump or dissipation vanishes.

Write $[v]_{i+1/2}=v_{i+1}-v_i$ and $[\psi]_{i+1/2}=\psi_{i+1}-\psi_i$, and use the arithmetic means in the definition of $\widehat q$. Then $-v_i^TF^{es}_{i+1/2}+\widehat q_{i+1/2}=\tfrac12[v]_{i+1/2}^TF^{es}_{i+1/2}-\tfrac12(\psi_i+\psi_{i+1})$ and $v_i^TF^{es}_{i-1/2}-\widehat q_{i-1/2}=\tfrac12[v]_{i-1/2}^TF^{es}_{i-1/2}+\tfrac12(\psi_{i-1}+\psi_i)$. At equal states the same formula gives $\widehat q=q$ by [F1] and the consistency in [F2], so this is a consistent numerical entropy flux. The right and left interface terms now combine with the entropy-jump defects from step 1.1.

By the chain rule and the semidiscrete update, $\Delta x\dot\eta(U_i)=-v_i^TF^{es}_{i+1/2}+v_i^TF^{es}_{i-1/2}$. Add $\widehat q_{i+1/2}-\widehat q_{i-1/2}$ and use step 2.1. The potential terms combine as $-\tfrac12(\psi_i+\psi_{i+1})+\tfrac12(\psi_{i-1}+\psi_i)=-\tfrac12([\psi]_{i+1/2}+[\psi]_{i-1/2})$. Hence $\Delta x$ times the cell residual equals $\tfrac12([v]_{i+1/2}^TF^{es}_{i+1/2}-[\psi]_{i+1/2})+\tfrac12([v]_{i-1/2}^TF^{es}_{i-1/2}-[\psi]_{i-1/2})$, which is nonpositive by step 1.1. This proves the local cell inequality; summing it on the periodic mesh cancels all numerical entropy fluxes. No time discretization was used.

$$\mathcal G_\gamma=\{(\rho,m,E):\rho>0,\ E>m^2/(2\rho)\}.$$

$$p(U)=(\gamma-1)\left(E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}\right)>0,$$
the velocity is $u=m/\rho$, and the flux is
$$F(U)=\left(m,\frac{m^2}{\rho}+p,\frac{m}{\rho}(E+p)\right).$$
The sound speed is $c=\sqrt{\gamma p/\rho}$. These definitions apply only
on $\mathcal G_\gamma$; a state with nonpositive density or nonpositive
internal energy is inadmissible. The set is open because $\rho$ and
$E-m^2/(2\rho)$ are continuous on $\rho>0$ and the inequalities are strict;
all displayed flux functions are smooth on this domain.

enclosing approximation to that fan, its admissibility hypothesis is that
every such speed lies in $[S_L,S_R]$; this definition supplies no general

Use the conservation-system convention of
[[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]]: on an open convex state
domain $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, the flux is $F:\mathcal A\to\mathbb R^m$.
A **convex entropy pair** is a pair $(\eta,q)$ with $\eta\in C^2(\mathcal A)$,
$q\in C^1(\mathcal A)$, positive-semidefinite Hessian $D^2\eta$, and
$$Dq(U)=D\eta(U)\,DF(U)\qquad(U\in\mathcal A).$$
The **entropy variable** is the column vector $v(U)=\nabla\eta(U)$; gradients
are represented as columns, so the compatibility equation above means
$\nabla q(U)=DF(U)^T v(U)$. The **entropy potential** is
$\psi(U)=v(U)^T F(U)-q(U)$. This definition does not assert that every convex
$\eta$ admits a flux $q$; the compatibility equation is part of the hypothesis.

Let $(\eta,q)$ be a convex entropy pair on an open domain $\mathcal A$, with
entropy variable $v$ and potential $\psi$ as in
[[def-pe03-system-entropy-pair-and-potential]]. A continuous two-point flux
$F^{ec}:\mathcal A\times\mathcal A\to\mathbb R^m$ is **entropy-conservative
in Tadmor's sense** if it is consistent and symmetric,
$F^{ec}(U,U)=F(U)$, and satisfies the exact jump identity
$$\bigl(v(U_R)-v(U_L)\bigr)^T F^{ec}(U_L,U_R)=\psi(U_R)-\psi(U_L)$$
for every pair $U_L,U_R\in\mathcal A$. This definition asserts no existence
for a prescribed entropy pair.

Let $(\eta,q)$ be an entropy pair with entropy variable $v$ and potential
$\psi$, and let $F^{ec}$ be a consistent entropy-conservative flux as in
[[def-pe03-tadmor-entropy-conservative-flux]]. For each pair
$(U_L,U_R)\in\mathcal A^2$, choose a symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix
$D(U_L,U_R)\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$. The associated **entropy-stable
dissipative flux** is
$$F^{es}(U_L,U_R):=F^{ec}(U_L,U_R)-\frac12D(U_L,U_R)(v(U_R)-v(U_L)).$$
Positive semidefinite means $z^TD(U_L,U_R)z\ge0$ for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$.
No fully discrete time-step property is included.

Let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be closed and convex (convex in the sense of
[[def-pe03-convex-invariant-domain]]), let $J$ be a finite nonempty
index set, let $w_j>0$ with $\sum_{j\in J}w_j=1$, and let input states
$V_j\in\mathbb R^m$ have mean $\bar V=\sum_jw_jV_j\in K$. The **maximal
convex scaling limiter** returns the largest $\theta\in[0,1]$ for which every
$$V_j^\theta=\bar V+\theta(V_j-\bar V)$$
belongs to $K$, together with all the states $V_j^\theta$. Equivalently, form
$$S=\{\theta\in[0,1]:V_j^\theta\in K\text{ for every }j\in J\},$$
and return $\theta_*:=\max S$ and $(V_j^{\theta_*})_{j\in J}$. The mean is
assumed admissible; implementation, cost, and any pointwise-in-cell property
are not part of this definition.

Fix $\gamma>1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, and use the state variables and internal
energy density from [[def-ideal-gas-euler-state-and-pressure]]. Define the
**positive-margin set**
$$K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}:=\left\{(\rho,m,E):\rho\ge\varepsilon,\quad E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}\ge\varepsilon\right\}.$$
Every member has positive density and positive pressure. Closedness and
convexity are proved in
[[prop-pe03-euler-state-and-margin-domains-are-convex-and-closed]]; those properties are not
being inferred from this definition alone.

Fix $\gamma>1$. In one space dimension the conserved state is
$U=(\rho,m,E)\in\mathbb R^3$, where $\rho$ is density, $m$ momentum, and
$E$ total energy per unit volume. The **admissible-state set** is the open set
$$\mathcal G_\gamma=\{(\rho,m,E):\rho>0,\ E>m^2/(2\rho)\}.$$
The ideal-gas pressure on this set is
$$p(U)=(\gamma-1)\left(E-\frac{m^2}{2\rho}\right)>0,$$
the velocity is $u=m/\rho$, and the flux is
$$F(U)=\left(m,\frac{m^2}{\rho}+p,\frac{m}{\rho}(E+p)\right).$$
The sound speed is $c=\sqrt{\gamma p/\rho}$. These definitions apply only
on $\mathcal G_\gamma$; a state with nonpositive density or nonpositive
internal energy is inadmissible. The set is open because $\rho$ and
$E-m^2/(2\rho)$ are continuous on $\rho>0$ and the inequalities are strict;
all displayed flux functions are smooth on this domain.

Fix $\gamma>1$, $\varepsilon>0$, a finite nonempty node set $J$, positive
weights $w_j$ summing to one, and candidate states $V_j\in\mathbb R^3$ with
mean $\bar V=\sum_jw_jV_j\in K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$. Apply the maximal
convex scaling limiter of
[[alg-pe03-convex-scaling-positivity-limiter]] with $K=K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$.
Its output is well-defined, every limited node lies in $K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$,
and the weighted cell mean remains $\bar V$. Hence every limited node has
positive density and positive pressure. If the unscaled nodes already lie in
$K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$, the maximal parameter is $\theta_*=1$. In
particular, if smooth target states stay a distance at least $\delta>0$ from
$\mathbb R^3\setminus K_{\gamma,\varepsilon}$ and each reconstruction node
has error less than $\delta$, the limiter is inactive and preserves that
reconstruction's accuracy. No positivity between finitely many nodes is
claimed.

Use the conservation-system convention of
[[def-hyperbolic-system-and-characteristic-families]]: on an open convex state
domain $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, the flux is $F:\mathcal A\to\mathbb R^m$.
A **convex entropy pair** is a pair $(\eta,q)$ with $\eta\in C^2(\mathcal A)$,
$q\in C^1(\mathcal A)$, positive-semidefinite Hessian $D^2\eta$, and
$$Dq(U)=D\eta(U)\,DF(U)\qquad(U\in\mathcal A).$$
The **entropy variable** is the column vector $v(U)=\nabla\eta(U)$; gradients
are represented as columns, so the compatibility equation above means
$\nabla q(U)=DF(U)^T v(U)$. The **entropy potential** is
$\psi(U)=v(U)^T F(U)-q(U)$. This definition does not assert that every convex
$\eta$ admits a flux $q$; the compatibility equation is part of the hypothesis.

Let $(\eta,q)$ be a convex entropy pair on an open domain $\mathcal A$, with
entropy variable $v$ and potential $\psi$ as in
[[def-pe03-system-entropy-pair-and-potential]]. A continuous two-point flux
$F^{ec}:\mathcal A\times\mathcal A\to\mathbb R^m$ is **entropy-conservative
in Tadmor's sense** if it is consistent and symmetric,
$F^{ec}(U,U)=F(U)$, and satisfies the exact jump identity
$$\bigl(v(U_R)-v(U_L)\bigr)^T F^{ec}(U_L,U_R)=\psi(U_R)-\psi(U_L)$$
for every pair $U_L,U_R\in\mathcal A$. This definition asserts no existence
for a prescribed entropy pair.

Let $(\eta,q)$ be an entropy pair with entropy variable $v$ and potential
$\psi$, and let $F^{ec}$ be a consistent entropy-conservative flux as in
[[def-pe03-tadmor-entropy-conservative-flux]]. For each pair
$(U_L,U_R)\in\mathcal A^2$, choose a symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix
$D(U_L,U_R)\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$. The associated **entropy-stable
dissipative flux** is
$$F^{es}(U_L,U_R):=F^{ec}(U_L,U_R)-\frac12D(U_L,U_R)(v(U_R)-v(U_L)).$$
Positive semidefinite means $z^TD(U_L,U_R)z\ge0$ for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$.
No fully discrete time-step property is included.

Let $(\eta,q)$ be a convex entropy pair on an open set $\mathcal A$, with
entropy variable $v$ and potential $\psi$ as in
[[def-pe03-system-entropy-pair-and-potential]]. On a periodic mesh of $N\ge2$
cells of width $\Delta x>0$, let differentiable states $U_i(t)\in\mathcal A$
satisfy
$$\dot U_i=-\frac{F^{es}_{i+1/2}-F^{es}_{i-1/2}}{\Delta x},$$
where every face flux is the entropy-stable dissipative flux of
[[def-pe03-entropy-stable-dissipative-flux]]. Define
$$\widehat q_{i+1/2}:=\left(\frac{v_i+v_{i+1}}2\right)^T F^{es}_{i+1/2}-\frac{\psi_i+\psi_{i+1}}2.$$
Then each cell satisfies
$$\frac{d}{dt}\eta(U_i)+\frac{\widehat q_{i+1/2}-\widehat q_{i-1/2}}{\Delta x}\le0.$$
Summing over the periodic mesh gives nonincrease of total discrete entropy.
This is a semidiscrete result; it asserts no entropy inequality for a chosen
fully discrete time integrator.

derivations.claim: The Rankine–Hugoniot speed from states $u_L=1,u_R=0$ is $(f(0)-f(1))/(0-1)=1/2$. Since $f'(0)=0<1/2<1=f'(1)$, it is a compressive shock. Its entropy production is $q(0)-q(1)-\tfrac12(\eta(0)-\eta(1))=-1/3+1/4=-1/12<0$, so it satisfies the quadratic entropy inequality.

The entropy-conservative Burgers flux is $f^{ec}=(u_L^2+u_Lu_R+u_R^2)/6$: it is symmetric and diagonal-consistent, and $(u_R-u_L)f^{ec}=(u_R^3-u_L^3)/6=[\psi]$, so [F2] applies. Hence $f^{ec}(1,0)=1/6$ and [F3] gives $f^{es}(1,0)=2/3$. With $[u]=-1$ and $[\psi]=-1/6$ from step 1.1, the Tadmor residual is $[u]f^{es}-[\psi]=-2/3+1/6=-1/2<0$.

Equal-state faces have flux $f^{es}(1,1)=1/2$ and $f^{es}(0,0)=0$ by [F2]–[F3]. Thus the left state adjacent to the jump updates to $1-\tfrac12(2/3-1/2)=11/12$, and the right state updates to $0-\tfrac12(0-2/3)=1/3$. The jump is spread over two intermediate values. This is a finite computation only; [F4] does not certify the forward-Euler step's entropy inequality. The interface flux value was obtained in step 2.1.
